The walking route reveals sweeping views of the cascades, the gorge and tropical vegetation. Mist rising from the falls and rainbows make every viewpoint feel different, while the Brazilian side offers particularly impressive views of the scale of the entire waterfall system.

The visit, entrance tickets and services are included in the main travel itinerary. Macuco Safari and the Bird Park take place on the same day and are presented as separate excursions.

From Cambará do Sul, you will travel to Itaimbezinho Canyon in a protected natural area. The rock walls, upland hills and lush vegetation unfold along the trails and from the viewpoints. There is time to spend a full day here, stopping to take in different views of the gorge.

In the afternoon, you will return to Cambará do Sul. On the VIP tour, the excursion is accompanied by an English-speaking guide.

On the journey from Lake Atitlán to Antigua, you will visit the archaeological site of Iximché, the former capital of the Kaqchikel Maya kingdom. A guide accompanies the visit.

Once in Antigua, you will explore this UNESCO World Heritage city. The walk takes in the principal streets and major landmarks of its colonial centre. On the Guatemala–Belize itinerary, the excursion ends in Antigua, where travellers stay overnight.

## Trails around Jardim da Amazônia Lodge

The walk follows forest trails around the lodge. Your guide introduces the local flora and fauna and explains the history of rubber extraction, which played an important role in the life of this region.

After the walk, enjoy a barbecue of fresh fish and relax in a hammock in the shade of the trees.

## Canoeing on the Claro River

The waterborne part of the itinerary follows the Claro River towards Anaconda Lake. The gentle current gives you time to admire the forest from the water and watch birds along the banks: kingfishers, herons, cormorants, tanagers and other species.

The walks on land and water complement each other: the trails provide a closer look at trees and plants, while the canoe opens up views of the forested riverbanks.

## Argentine Side of Iguazu Falls

With a Russian-speaking guide, you will set off for the Argentine side of the falls. The journey from Brazil crosses the Iguazu River via Tancredo Neves Bridge.

Inside the national park, paths and walkways lead above the cascades to viewpoints beside the falling water. Here you hear the roar of the torrents, while mist rises over the gorge. During the walk, you will see Devil's Throat and the falls from different heights.

The walking trails offer close-up views of the cascades and a chance to discover the nature of the surrounding park.

## Price

The excursion costs $123. The entrance ticket costs $40 and is paid separately.
